body:
## Summary
When deriving `food_expenditures`/`food_quantities`/`food_prices`, the build path (`country.py` ~L2100, `run_make_target` / `_FOOD_DERIVED`) tries to `make` the `food_acquired.parquet` target **first**, then falls back to the Python/YAML build. For **YAML-path** `food_acquired` countries (e.g. Mali) there is no make rule, so each call emits a cascade of:
```
make: *** No rule to make target '…/food_acquired.parquet'.  Stop.
UserWarning: Makefile execution failed for Mali/2014-15 food_acquired: …returned non-zero exit status 2.
```
before the YAML fallback runs. The warnings are misleading — they imply the country uses a Makefile build when it doesn't — and they fire several times per country (per candidate path).

A related case: **Nepal** (and other no-microdata countries) produce the same cascade because no source data exists, ending in `RuntimeError: Could not materialize …`.

## Repro
```python
import lsms_library as ll
ll.Feature('food_expenditures')()   # screenfuls of "No rule to make target …" for Mali/Nepal/etc.
```

## Suggested fix
- Probe for a make rule (or a known YAML-path declaration) **before** attempting `make`, so YAML-path features go straight to the Python build without the spurious "No rule to make target" warnings.
- Demote the make-miss to debug-level (or suppress) when a successful fallback follows.
- For known no-microdata countries (Nepal, Armenia — see CLAUDE.md "Countries Without Microdata"), short-circuit the food-derivation with a single clear "no source data" notice rather than a multi-path `make` cascade.

Cosmetic / UX only — no incorrect data results; the fallbacks ultimately succeed where data exists.
title: food-derivation: noisy 'No rule to make target …food_acquired.parquet' for YAML-path / no-data countries
